faculty_override_note: The official two-year, four-semester map is the default. The official five-semester map is an alternate lighter-load pathway. DegreeWorks and faculty advisement remain authoritative. This plan assumes the HIS 101/HIS 102 sequence pair by default; a student pursuing the HIS 115/HIS 116 or HIS 120/HIS 125 pair should adjust the plan with an advisor (see sequence_notes).
sequence_notes: The required History Sequence is enforced as one linked pair: HIS 101 and HIS 102, HIS 115 and HIS 116, or HIS 120 and HIS 125. Mixed pairs do not satisfy the requirement.
HIS 275 requires ENG 201 plus completion of a valid History Sequence pair; both conditions are enforced.

At least one History elective must be a non-Western History course. The eligible set follows the asterisked courses in the official degree maps: HIS 114, HIS 121, HIS 122, HIS 126, HIS 129, HIS 130, HIS 131, or HIS 226.
PHI 100 is the shown Individual and Society course; ECO 100 is listed as its alternate.
Select any Creative Expression Pathways course other than SPE 100 or SPE 102 for the second Creative Expression requirement.
Students are advised (not required) to complete 1 course from AFN/HIS 123, AFN/HIS 124, ASN 114, HED 195, HIS 120, HIS 125, or POL 100 for U.S. Experience in Its Diversity.
Students are strongly encouraged (not required) to take a modern language course to satisfy World Cultures and Global Issues.
SPE 102 is the listed alternate to SPE 100 for non-native speakers of English.

A total of 6 credits (2 courses) from AFL, AFN, ANT, ASN, ECO, GEO, HIS, LAT, PHI, POL, PSY, or SOC is required for the Social Science or Ethnic Studies elective; an Ethnic Studies course is an explicit alternate option.
A total of 6 credits (2 courses) of General Elective is required; a 300-level English course, a Health Education course, and/or Modern Language course(s) are recommended but not required.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
